title: Singular-element witnesses in the height-zero auxiliary algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A,C$ finitely presented commutative $R$-algebras, and $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra. Let $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$, $\beta:A\to C$, $\gamma:C\to\Lambda$ be $R$-algebra homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] with $\gamma\beta=\alpha$. Let $s\subset A$ be a finite subset of $H_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $n:s\to\mathbb N$, and $\ell:s\to\Lambda$ with $\ell(a)\alpha(a)^{n(a)}=0$ for every $a\in s$. Let $c\in H_{C/R}$. Then there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ and maps $\beta\prime:A\to B$, $\delta:B\to\Lambda$ with $\delta\beta\prime=\alpha$, an element $b\in H_{B/R}$ with $\delta(b)=(\prod_{a\in s}\ell(a))\gamma(c)$, and, for every $a\in s$, an element $d_a\in H_{B/R}$ with $\delta(d_a)=\alpha(a)^{n(a)+1}$. The carrier of $C$ and of $B$ is taken in the maximum of the universes of $R,A$.

source.place: Lemma 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), auxiliary polynomial quotient and its two localizations; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FA

proof.text: A is Noetherian. Give C its A-algebra structure through beta; its finitely many R-algebra generators also generate it over A. Since A is Noetherian this is a finite presentation: choose C = A[x_k]/(f_j) and a polynomial lift p of c.

Put L = product_i ell_i. Because ell_i annihilates alpha(a_i)^(n_i) and divides L, L annihilates each such power. Construct B = A[x_k,y_i,z,t_ij]/(f_j - sum_i y_i t_ij, z y_i). Evaluate x_k through C, y_i at alpha(a_i)^(n_i), z at L, t_ij at zero. Both families of relations vanish, so the quotient universal property produces delta with delta beta_prime = alpha. B is finite type over R and hence finitely presented. This is an explicit quotient construction, not a definition selecting a witness from a holed existence theorem.

Let c_prime be the class of p. The first auxiliary localization identifies B_z with C[t_ij,z]_z respecting c_prime. Further localization at c_prime is smooth over the smooth R-algebra C_c. Iterated localization identifies this with B_(z*c_prime); hence b = z*c_prime lies in H_{B/R}. Its image is L*gamma(c). If s is empty, B = C[z], and this argument uses the direct polynomial description instead of the auxiliary lemma with r >= 1.

For each a_i in s, the second auxiliary localization identifies B_(y_i) with a localized polynomial algebra over A. Further localization at a_i is smooth over A_(a_i), which is smooth over R. Iterated localization therefore makes B_(beta_prime(a_i)*y_i) smooth over R. Thus d_i = beta_prime(a_i)*y_i lies in H_{B/R} and delta(d_i) = alpha(a_i)^(n_i+1). For s empty this assertion is vacuous. Exponents zero cause no problem: the annihilation hypothesis then says ell_i = 0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_height_zero_auxiliary_witnesses
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {Λ : Type t} {C : Type (max u v)}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R C]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [FinitePresentation R A] [FinitePresentation R C]
    (α : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (β : A →ₐ[R] C) (γ : C →ₐ[R] Λ)
    (hcomp : γ.comp β = α) (s : Finset A)
    (hs : ∀ a ∈ s, a ∈ singularIdeal R A)
    (n : s → ℕ) (ell : s → Λ)
    (hkill : ∀ a : s, ell a * α a.val ^ n a = 0)
    (c : C) (hc : c ∈ singularIdeal R C) :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B),
      ∃ (β' : A →ₐ[R] B) (δ : B →ₐ[R] Λ),
        FinitePresentation R B ∧ δ.comp β' = α ∧
        (∃ b ∈ singularIdeal R B, δ b = (∏ a : s, ell a) * γ c) ∧
        (∀ a : s, ∃ d ∈ singularIdeal R B, δ d = α a.val ^ (n a + 1))
